paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the LORD sees, and the LORD judges. David sings that God sits on His throne "judging righteously" and that He "judges the world with justice" (Psalm 9:4, 8). Then comes the question that hits close to home: "Why, O LORD, do You stand far off? Why do You hide in times of trouble?" (Psalm 10:1). Notice that the psalm doesn't hide that question, because it sings it right to God.

Look at the two voices in this psalm, baker: the wicked man tells himself, "God has forgotten; He hides His face and never sees" (Psalm 10:11). But the psalmist says God has "regarded trouble and grief" and that "You are the helper of the fatherless" (Psalm 10:14). One of those two is wrong, and it's NOT the one holding on to God! When trouble makes you feel unseen, don't let that feeling do the talking, because David says, "You, O LORD, have not forsaken those who seek You" (Psalm 9:10).

So what do you do with this today? Run to Him, friend, because "The LORD is a refuge for the oppressed, a stronghold in times of trouble" (Psalm 9:9), and the cry of the afflicted is something He "does not ignore" (Psalm 9:12). Bring Him the hard questions, bring Him the hurt, and bring Him the praise too. I give thanks to the LORD with ALL my heart, and I hope you do too, because "The LORD is King forever and ever" (Psalm 10:16).
